dispositions.topic_text: Installation gate and evidence for rejecting non-Linux hosts before startup
dispositions.what: Where installation refuses a host whose kernel is not Linux's (installer preflight, deployment-platform constraint, or both), as State 2 rounds 133 T2 and 134 T4 carried. Every option must keep A20 Required test 7: installing on a non-Linux kernel fails and no instance starts, checked outside Registry's code.
keeps:
Installing a release on a host whose kernel is not Linux's fails, and no
   instance of it starts (rule 6).
options: Have the installer inspect the host kernel before installing or starting the service.
Constrain the deployment platform to Linux and have deployment admission reject every other platform.
Use both an installer preflight and a deployment-platform constraint.
A pre-start deployment check reads the host kernel identity and refuses to launch the container or process.
The container runtime declares Linux as a hard platform constraint and installation verifies the selected platform.
Both deployment preflight and runtime-platform constraints enforce it.
consequences: Installer inspection makes the refusal explicit but depends on the install entrypoint always being used.
Platform admission centralizes enforcement but requires every deployment path to pass through it.
Both checks provide defense in depth at the cost of duplicated policy.
A preflight check gives a direct diagnostic but must run before any instance starts.
A platform constraint is declarative but depends on the installer honoring it.
Both reduce accidental bypass at the cost of duplicated enforcement.
